## {.center background-image="img/earth-from-space.png" data-menu-title="Earth from space"}

::: notes

## 100+ petabytes of data

::: {.columns}
::::: {.column width="40%"}
![](img/NISAR.png){.absolute .no-radius height=400px left=-120px top=290px style="transform: rotate(90deg);"}
:::::

::::: {.column width="60%"}
::::::: daacs
![](img/DAACS1.png){.no-radius width="1100px"}

![](img/DAACS2.png){.no-radius width="1100px"}

![](img/DAACS3.png){.no-radius width="1100px"}
:::::::
:::::
:::

::: notes
- NASA's Earth Science program manages over 100 petabytes of remote sensing data
- contributes to scientific research all over the world,
- helping us learn about climate change and its impacts, landscape and ocean biology, and water and atmospheric processes.
- Really important things for the future of the world
- Scientists need to get it, understand it, use it
- Getting this data into the hands of scientists is a complicated task that is the primary responsibility of NASA staff across 11 different data centres.
:::

## {.center background-image="img/mentors.png" data-menu-title="Mentors" visibility="hidden"}

##

::: {.center-x}
![](img/cloud-shift.png)
:::

::: notes
- This task has changed over the last few years
- Like so many organisations, moved data from on-premesis servers to the cloud
- Many advantages
- Access patterns to the data have changed
- Important that researchers can still easily access the data
- Data centre staff have been challenged to both learn and teach new and more efficient ways of accessing and working with cloud-based satellite data.
:::

![](img/earthdata-cookbook-hex.png){width="70%"}

## Technical & Social Infrastructure Together

![](img/openscapes_hex.png){.absolute height=220px left=1339px top=-36px}

![](img/people-tooling.png){.absolute height=598px left=70px top=231.7px}

- **Beautiful feedback loop**
- Using similar infrastructure promotes and streamlines teamwork.
- Teamwork better equips you to learn new infrastructure.
- Openscapes provides scaffolding and space and facilitation to spin this wheel.
:::

## NASA Openscapes Mentors

::: columns
::::: {.column width="40%" .center-x}
![](img/nasa-logo.png){width="40%"} ![](img/openscapes_hex.png){width="30%"}

![](img/daacs-logos.png)
:::::

::::: {.column width="60%"}
![](img/mentors.png){width="100%"}
:::::
:::

::: notes
- Working with NASA since 2021 to support Data Center staff in their migration to the cloud
- Data Center staff teach workshops on cloud data access, and from these produce amazing tutorials
- combining best practices for cloud data access, analysis, and scientific context
- a critical resource for users, BUT
- Data Centers were doing this in silos
  - duplicated effort
  - Not learning from each other
- Openscapes has been working with mentors to build a framework for collaboration so they can build these tutorials together.
:::

::: notes
- Multilingual \-
  - Meet contributors where they are and meet needs of diverse users
  - Contribute via ipynb or qmd, Python or R
  - Standardized format look/feel
- Quarto file format
  - Contributors seeing benefits over ipynb (slowly) \+1
  - Plain text file (?)
  - easy to version control, easy to review (difficult with ipynb)
- Multi-format download (ipynb) (people like notebooks)
- Publishing tools
  - GitHub pages
  - Freeze
    - Don't need to execute whole book
:::

# Collaborative coworking is a force multiplier

::: notes
- We are in a Quarto session, and I want to emphasize how critical Quarto has been
- But I also want to make sure to center the Mentors at NASA, and their passion, expertise, and leadership.
- Talk about the collaborative coworking that has been a critical part of the success of the cookbook.
:::

## What is coworking?

::: {.columns}
::::: {.column width="60%" .v-center}
![](img/Zoomie_MentorsRetreat2024_NASA-Openscapes.png)
:::::

::::: {.column width="40%"}
![](img/coworking-doc.png)
:::::
:::

::: notes
- Biweekly hour and a half session, on Zoom, with NASA Mentors
- come together to work on the cookbook
- Openscapes provides scaffolding: **scheduling**, **Zoom**, creating **shared notes** docs
- I lead these sessions, looking out for what they need
- Discuss what needs to be done / what we want to work on
- Match up expertise / interest with needs - **Breakout rooms**
- Design and create **new content**
- Create **issues**, Review **PRs**
- **Onboard** new contributors
- **Screenshare** to get feedback or solve a problem together.
- Seeing how other people work is a big part of transition to working more openly and collaboratively.
- **Quarto** tool that doesn't require too much effort to learn **makes coworking easier**
:::
